title: bug: propose_rail records the task's assignee as the proposer, not the caller, so a governor's or QA's proposal shows up as the worker's
description:
Observed on 2026-10-30 at 11:41Z. governor-693b7073 called moe.propose_rail on task-de91373a, which worker-c2da129d had been assigned at 11:40:59Z. The stored proposal, prop-4fe44aac98c545819e94ed8e3f581e0b, records workerId "worker-c2da129d". The worker's own proposal, prop-da2a6c91, records the same id. In the IDE it therefore looks as if the worker filed the same waiver twice.

Cause: packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/proposeRail.ts:67 sets `workerId: task.assignedWorkerId || 'unknown'`. The tool's inputSchema has no workerId property (additionalProperties: false), so the caller's identity is never read. The proxy auto-injects workerId for the tools whose schema declares it, as moe.set_task_dependencies does.

Fix: add the optional `workerId` input ("Caller worker ID (auto-injected by proxy)") and record the caller as the proposer. Fall back to the assignee, then 'unknown', only when no caller id is supplied. Update the moe.propose_rail section of docs/MCP_SERVER.md, and docs/SCHEMA.md if it describes Proposal.workerId.

Out of scope: proposal approval paths, the IDE rendering, and existing stored proposals.
definitionOfDone: moe.propose_rail called with a workerId that differs from the task's assignee stores that caller's id as the proposal's workerId. Shown by a test in packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/proposeRail.test.ts.
A call without workerId still records the task's assignee (or 'unknown'), unchanged. Shown by a test.
The moe.propose_rail section of docs/MCP_SERVER.md documents the workerId input, and `cd packages/moe-daemon && npm test` exits 0.
